Russell Grigg is a British historian and Senior Lecturer (Primary) in Initial Teacher Education, Education and Childhood Studies at Swansea University.
He is known for his works on the history of education, teacher education and school inspection.
He has been an education inspector for the Ministry of Education (United Arab Emirates). Previously he was an associate professor at the Wales Centre for Equity in Education.
Books
* Lewis, H. & Grigg, R. (2023). Dogs in Schools: Pedagogy and Practice for Happy, Healthy, and Humane Interventions (1st ed.), Routledge.
* Grigg, R. (2023). The Little Book of Pembrokeshire, The History Press.
*
* Grigg, R. (2022). Becoming an Outstanding Primary School Teacher, Routledge.
* Grigg, R. (2022). Little Book of Carmarthenshire, The History Press.
* Lewis, H. & Grigg, R. (2020). Tails from the Classroom: Learning and teaching through animal-assisted interventions (1st ed.). Crown House Publishing Ltd.
* Grigg, R. & Lewis, H. (2018). Teaching Creative and Critical Thinking in Schools, SAGE Publications Ltd.
* Grigg, R. & Hughes, S. (2018). Teaching Primary Humanities (2nd ed.). Routledge.
* Grigg, R. & Lewis, H. (2018). Teaching on a Shoestring: An A–Z of everyday objects to enthuse and engage children and extend learning in the early years, Crown House.
* Grigg, R. (2016). Big Ideas in Education: What every teacher should know (1st ed.). Crown House Publishing.
* Grigg, R. & Lewis, H. (2016). A to Z of Learning Outside the Classroom (1st ed.). Bloomsbury Education.
* Grigg, R. (1998). History of Trinity College, Carmarthen, 1848-1998, University of Wales Press.
